questions.q: What does “doblar a la derecha” mean?
questions.explain: “Doblar a la derecha” means “to turn right”.

questions.q: What does 'navegar por internet' mean?
questions.explain: 'Navegar por internet' means 'to surf/browse the internet'.

questions.q: How do you say “We must protect the planet”?
questions.explain: “Proteger” = to protect and “el planeta” is masculine: “Hay que proteger el planeta”.

questions.q: What does “está a las afueras, lejos del centro” describe about a place?
options: It is on the outskirts, far from the centre
It is right in the town centre
questions.explain: “Lejos del centro” means “far from the centre”, so the place is on the outskirts.

questions.q: What does “navegar por internet” mean?
questions.explain: “Navegar por internet” is the idiom “to surf/browse the internet”.

questions.q: How do you say “The flight was cancelled because of the weather”?
options: El vuelo se canceló a causa del tiempo
El viaje se canceló a causa del tiempo
El vuelo se cancela a causa del tiempo
El vuelo salió a causa del tiempo
questions.explain: “El vuelo” = the flight, “se canceló” = was cancelled and “a causa del tiempo” = because of the weather.

questions.q: How do you say 'I spend too much time on my mobile'?
options: Paso demasiado tiempo en el ordenador
Paso poco tiempo en el móvil
Gasto demasiado dinero en el móvil
Paso demasiado tiempo en el móvil
questions.explain: 'Pasar tiempo' = 'to spend time' (use 'gastar' only for money); 'demasiado' = 'too much'.

questions.q: What does “el equipaje de mano” mean?
questions.explain: “El equipaje” = luggage and “de mano” = hand, so “el equipaje de mano” = “hand luggage”.

questions.q: What does “la panadería” mean?
questions.explain: “La panadería” (from “pan”, bread) means “the bakery”.

questions.q: What does “la sequía” mean?
questions.explain: “La sequía” means “drought”, a long period without rain.

questions.q: What does “el ayuntamiento” mean?
questions.explain: “El ayuntamiento” means “the town hall”, the local council building.

questions.q: Which means 'I will travel to Spain next year' (future)?
options: Viajé a España el año pasado
Viajaré a España el año que viene
questions.explain: 'Viajaré' is the future tense 'I will travel'; with 'el año que viene' (next year) the future is correct.

questions.q: What does “un programa concurso” mean?
questions.explain: “Un programa concurso” means “a game show / quiz show” on television.

questions.q: What does “sigue todo recto” mean when giving directions?
questions.explain: “Seguir todo recto” means “to go straight on”.

questions.q: What does “la cocina” mean?
questions.explain: “La cocina” means “the kitchen” (it can also mean “the cooker”).

questions.q: Which means “I'd recommend visiting the old town”?
questions.explain: “El casco antiguo” means “the old town”, and “recomendaría” is the conditional “I'd recommend”.

questions.q: How do you say “I prefer subtitles to dubbing”?
options: Prefiero los subtítulos a la pantalla
Prefiero el doblaje a los subtítulos
questions.explain: “Los subtítulos” = subtitles and “el doblaje” = dubbing: “Prefiero los subtítulos al doblaje”.

questions.q: Which sentence means “The internet keeps me informed”?
questions.explain: “Mantener informado” = “to keep informed”, so “Internet me mantiene informado”.

questions.q: What does “la librería” mean?
questions.explain: “La librería” is a false friend: it means “bookshop”, while “library” is “la biblioteca”.

questions.q: How do you say 'My favourite singer is very famous'?
options: Mi cantante favorito está muy famoso
Mi cantante favorito es muy hambriento
Mi cantante favorito es muy famoso
Mi cantante favorita es muy famoso
questions.explain: 'Es' is used for permanent fame, and 'favorito/famoso' agree as masculine: 'Mi cantante favorito es muy famoso'.

questions.q: What does 'seguir a un influencer en las redes sociales' mean?
options: To follow an influencer on social media
questions.explain: 'Seguir' means 'to follow', so this means 'to follow an influencer on social media'.

questions.q: How do you say 'I live in a quiet neighbourhood'?
questions.explain: 'El barrio' is masculine, so 'tranquilo' agrees; 'vivo' is the correct first-person form.
